note.question: What determines healthcare and public services?
note.overview: A continuum of customers simultaneously selects facilities to minimize travel plus congestion cost, producing a nonatomic Wardrop-type demand equilibrium; a provider then uses service-rate choices to shape that equilibrium.

source.quote: The exogenous Poisson arrival assumption implies that demand at each location x arises independently of other locations; roughly speaking, the arrival process in each infinitesimal subregion is an independent renewal process.
Thus, the arrival rate to each queue will be determined endog­ enously by the set of customers who prefer that facility to others.

We study the equilibrium using a queueing model in which customers arrive according to a spatiotemporal Poisson process (not only at random times but at ran­ dom locations), and each facility is represented by an M/M/1 queue.

components.label: Unique nonatomic spatial demand
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Unique nonatomic spatial demand (Wardrop) equilibrium. Customer assignments satisfy minimum generalized cost and congestion consistency. Theorem 1 on PDF p. 5 proves existence, and Theorem 2 on the same page proves uniqueness. Theorem 3 on PDF p. 6 gives comparative statics. Theorems 4-6 on PDF pp. 7, 9-10 characterize the social partition and conditions under which optimized service rates decentralize it.
